profile.name: Denia
profile.review:
Denia is a 5-star Fusion Rectifier Hybrid character who plays into the Fusion Burst and Tune Strain team archetypes. By either focusing on strong Fusion Burst application and related team-wide buffs, or an even stronger buffing profile for Tune Strain hypercarries depending on her mode, she deals a lot of damage, rotates quickly, and has a highly specialized but equally as powerful buffing profile, featuring constant off-field grouping as well for maximal performance in both AoE and single-target situations in the teams she plays in. Let’s figure out how all of it works so we can squeeze the maximum performance out of her combat gameplay.

Resonance Mode explanation

Denia plays into either Tune Strain or Fusion Burst depending on her Resonance Mode (configurable at will before combat). They modify the following aspects of her kit:

  • Her “Etched Colors” Inherent Skill (can either increase party-wide Fusion DMG or Tune Break Boost);

  • Most of the attacks in her kit will either apply 1 stack of Fusion Burst or Tune Strain - Shifting and reset the duration of Tune Strain - Interfered;

  • In Tune Strain mode, she may fill each target’s Tune Break gauge by 50% of the max once per enemy per battle;

  • Her Outro skill changes to either amplify party-wide Fusion Burst DMG or general DMG Amplification (15 to 40% depending on whether the buffed character can apply Tune Strain or not);

  • In Tune Strain mode, she obtains standard Tune Strain - Interfered response like Qingxiao, Lynae, Mornye or Luuk.

  • Some Sequences are also impacted, but we will only cover her S0 kit here.

Key Mechanics, Rotation & Buffs

Other than her Resonance Mode, Denia’s in-game combat focus will be on accessing her second Ultimate, “Final Act - Breakdown Form”. Speaking of which, she has 2 forms she may switch between via her Ultimates: Stagecraft Form and Breakdown Form. In practice, Stagecraft Form only serves to fill the gauge Breakdown Form will utilize in order to increase the damage of attacks in that form as well as the speed at which she can access her Second Ultimate. 

For this purpose, Denia has several Forte resources that we won’t spend too much time detailing, as her standard rotations cover all of Denia’s bases in both Resonance Modes and in both casual play and quickswap, so we will only focus on the moves her standard rotation will utilize, as follows;

Her Intro in Stagecraft Form refills a bit of “Void Particle” Forte gauge and Concerto; the same applies for her Stagecraft Form Skill and Basic 4 (accessed immediately after Intro);

She then consumes it via her Basic Attacks in Breakdown Form (after switching to it via her Ultimate) to access her 2 Skills;

Casting both Breakdown Form skills will allow her to perform her second Ultimate, placing an Erosion Field that constantly spins on the ground and applies Fusion Burst or Tune Strain while grouping enemies periodically, and she is then free to switch out.

The summary above essentially constitutes the main concepts of Denia’s rotation that will grant the following buffs to the team:

  • Fusion Burst application (via a lot of her attacks and periodically off-field via her second Ultimate), constant off-field grouping (via second Ultimate), Fusion Burst DMG Amplification (via Outro) and Fusion DMG Bonus (via Echo Set and Inherent Skill) in Fusion Burst mode;

  • Tune Strain application and duration refresh (via a lot of her attacks and periodically off-field via her Second Ultimate), constant off-field grouping (via Second Ultimate), general DMG Amplification significantly increased if the target ally applies Tune Strain (via Outro) and Tune Break Boost (and some ATK% via Echo set effects and Inherent Skill).

Additionally, her Signature Weapon can also boost the ATK of the team if acquired!

Meta Position & Conclusion

Denia has significant personal damage, a very specialized and equally capable buffing profile, and a fast rotation. All of these factors undeniably make her the prime Secondary choice for the teams that she plays in. However, this comes at a cost: specialization.

Denia is highly specialized towards Tune Strain and Fusion Burst teams, since most of her buffs are tailored to characters of only that archetype. While her personal DMG, general DMG Amplification capability on Outro (even if weakened) and her generalist buffs via Echo sets like Moonlit Clouds and her Signature weapon definitely exist and could make you think she has a strong general use case, she’s nowhere near comparable to a proper generalist character like Lynae, or a less specialized support like Iuno for Heavy Attacks. This is her main (and realistically, only) flaw, aside from needing to change Echo sets in between each team, which can definitely cause build complications if you want to lean into her (albeit small) team flexibility.

As of her release, all Denia has access to is Fusion Burst teams with Aemeath and Tune Strain teams with Qingxiao or Luuk Herssen, only giving her a total of 2 teams that she can play in with no certainty of additional teams coming in the future. However, the 2 team archetypes that she does play in are very strong in the current meta, work well in both single-target and AoE thanks to her, and overall, if you wish to have any of her DPS but they lack a proper premium team, and you wish to pick up a strong power upgrade to either your Aemeath, Qingxiao or Luuk, Denia is the perfect opportunity to do this. It’s however worth noting that Mornye in specific is a particular necessity as a support to her Tune Strain teams, and without her she has a hard time performing at the expected top level performance Denia and a Tune Strain DPS are supposed to give (Lynae is better when used with alternative supports, but Denia is the best Tune Strain specialist we have).

In conclusion, while Denia is un”denia”bly (I swear I’m funny) a highly specialized secondary buffer and damage dealer character, in the teams that she is specialized for, she’s by all accounts ideal and will make your premium Fusion Burst and Tune Strain DPS characters unleash their full potential and be top tier provided you have the correct teammates to surround them.
profile.pros:
• Integral part of several meta teams, the uncontested best in slot for Fusion Burst and Tune Strain teams;

  • Has lots of viable weapon alternatives in Fusion Burst mode;

  • Constant off-field grouping making even single-target oriented DPSes excel in AoE scenarios;

  • Fast rotation, high damage, strong buffs and utility. Has all the markings of a top-tier secondary buffer/damage dealer.
profile.cons:
• Only plays into 2 team archetypes, both limited in Support options. If you don’t have either team, she has no flexibility to speak of;

  • Significantly more Signature weapon-dependent if used in Tune Strain mode, becomes a pretty recommended pick-up. Additionally non-negotiably needs Mornye in that mode;

  • Uses 3 different Echo Sets based on her team. Even her own flexibility is limited by needing multiple builds in each, however this is mitigated if you only plan to use her for one team archetype.

profile.rotations:
Rotation & Gameplay

Some ability names written in the rotations have been shortened for ease of comprehension.

The focus of Denia’s kit is to generate 100 points of Void Particle to then consume it in Breakdown Form by switching into it via her Ultimate and casting Basic Attacks, to finally cast her 2 Skills and second Ultimate and then Outro. It makes her rotation look like this:

Echo Timing

At any point in the rotation (Fusion Burst with Reminiscence: Denia or Lioness of Glory) or Swap Cancelled right before switching out following Ultimate: Breakdown via Outro (Tune Strain with Voidwing Moth).

Standard Rotation

  • Intro

  • Basic: Stagecraft 4 (Cancel animation endlag via Skill)

  • Skill: Phantom Bubble (Cancel animation instantly via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate: Stagecraft

  • Basic: Breakdown 1

  • Basic: Breakdown 2 (Cancel animation endlag via Jump)

  • Jump

  • Basic: Breakdown Midair 1

  • Basic: Breakdown Midair 2 (Cancel animation endlag via Skill)

  • Skill: Banish 1

  • Skill: Banish 2 (Cancel animation instantly via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate: Breakdown

  • Outro

This uses Denia’s potential for animation cancels to the fullest and ensures a fast rotation that accomplishes all of her goals. However, Denia can rotate more easily than this by simply doing 4 Basic Attacks without any Jump Cancels in Breakdown Form. This loses a bit of time, but is much easier to perform and applies some extra instances of Tune Strain or Fusion Burst depending on her mode.However, Denia can also, in the Aemeath + Lupa team, be the first character to rotate in the team. Were that to be the case, she’d need to generate extra Forte points to still have her Breakdown Form enhanced like so:

Opener Rotation

Used once only in Aemeath + Lupa + Denia (or any team where Denia rotates first)

  • Basic: Stagecraft 1 (Cancel animation endlag via Skill)

  • Skill: Phantom Bubble (Cancel animation instantly via Dash)

  • Dash

  • Basic: Stagecraft 1

  • Basic: Stagecraft 2

  • Basic: Stagecraft 3

  • Basic: Stagecraft 4 (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate: Stagecraft

  • Basic: Breakdown 1

  • Basic: Breakdown 2 (Cancel animation endlag via Jump)

  • Jump

  • Basic: Breakdown Midair 1

  • Basic: Breakdown Midair 2 (Cancel animation endlag via Skill)

  • Skill: Banish 1

  • Skill: Banish 2 (Cancel animation instantly via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate: Breakdown

  • Outro

Sequences & further optimization

Denia’s S3 makes her able to go directly into Breakdown Form upon switching into the field. This means that she can go Intro → Ultimate in the standard rotation, or start directly with her Ultimate on her Opener rotation. This can save 1 to 2.7s depending on the rotation used (Loop/Opener).

Additionally, Denia is free to utilize quickswaps during her Breakdown Form basics. This means you can swap out of - for example - her Breakdown Form Basic 2, and switch back into her later to cast Basic 3 and 4 and finish the rotation that way. She can also cast Stagecraft Form Basic Attacks to generate Forte ahead of time, overall making her rotations short, flexible and quickswap-friendly. Experiment depending on your team and feel free to see what works best!

skills.name: "Flawless"
skills.description:
Erosion Field

  • After casting Resonance Liberation Final Act - Breakdown Form, generate an Erosion Field, lasting for 30s. Only one Erosion Field generated by your own Resonator can exist at a time.

  • Erosion Field pulls in nearby targets once every 4s, dealing Fusion DMG, considered Resonance Liberation DMG.

Void Particle

  • When in the Breakdown Form while holding Void Particle, Normal Attack consumes Void Particle on hit and grants the following effects:

    • The skill DMG is considered Resonance Liberation DMG and the DMG Multiplier is increased by 50%.

    • Conformal Charge regenerates 100% faster.

Resonance Mode - Fusion Burst

  • While in Resonance Mode - Fusion Burst, Denia gains the following effects:

    • Each time when the following skills deal damage, inflict 2 stacks of Fusion Burst on the target. The same skill can only trigger this effect once every 2s against the same target.

      • Intro Skill It's Been A While!, Intro Skill Knock Knock, Resonance Liberation Final Act - Stagecraft Form, Resonance Liberation Final Act - Breakdown Form, and Erosion Field.

    • Each time when the following skills deal damage, inflict Fusion Burst on the target. The same skill can only trigger this effect once every 2s against the same target.

      • Basic Attack - Stagecraft Form Stage 3, Basic Attack - Stagecraft Form Stage 4, Basic Attack - Breakdown Form Stage 3, Basic Attack - Breakdown Form Stage 4, Mid-air Attack - Breakdown Form Stage 3, and Mid-air Attack - Breakdown Form Stage 4.

    • When Denia is in the team, if an enemy falls to Fusion Burst DMG, it counts as caused by the nearest active Resonator.

Resonance Mode - Tune Strain

  • While in Resonance Mode - Tune Strain, Denia gains the following effects:

    • Each time when the following skills deal damage, inflict Tune Strain - Shifting on the target and reset the duration of Tune Strain - Interfered on the target. The same skill can only trigger this effect once every 2s against the same target.

      • Intro Skill It's Been A While!, Intro Skill Knock Knock, Resonance Liberation Final Act - Stagecraft Form, Resonance Liberation Final Act - Breakdown Form, Erosion Field, Basic Attack - Stagecraft Form Stage 3, Basic Attack - Stagecraft Form Stage 4, Basic Attack - Breakdown Form Stage 3, Basic Attack - Breakdown Form Stage 4, Mid-air Attack - Breakdown Form Stage 3 and Mid-air Attack - Breakdown Form Stage 4.

    • When Resonators in the team inflict Tune Strain - Shifting on the target, this target's Off-Tune Level is increased by 50% of the max. This effect can only be triggered on the same target once every 300s.

Dark Core

  • Denia can hold up to 3 Dark Cores.

  • While in the Entropy Shift states, Denia obtains 1 Dark Cores every 12s.

  • Denia obtains 1 Dark Cores upon casting Intro Skill It's Been A While! and Intro Skill Knock Knock.

Void Particle

  • Denia can hold up to 100 points of Void Particle.

  • While in Stagecraft Form, dealing damage through Normal Attack grants Void Particle.

  • Casting Intro Skill It's Been A While!, Intro Skill Knock Knock or Resonance Skill Phantom Bubble - Stagecraft Form grants 25 points of Void Particle.

Conformal Charge

  • Denia can hold up to 100 points of Conformal Charge.

  • While in Breakdown Form, dealing damage through Normal Attack or Resonance Skill Beckon - Breakdown Form grants Conformal Charge.

  • Casting Resonance Skill Banish - Breakdown Form Stage 2 grants 40 points of Conformal Charge.

skills.name: Unfinished Lies
skills.description:
When in Resonance Mode - Fusion Burst, Fusion Burst DMG against targets near the active Resonator in the team is Amplified by 60% for 30s.

This effect ends early when Denia switches modes.

When in Resonance Mode - Tune Strain, the incoming Resonator has their All DMG Amplified by 15% for 16s.

After this Resonator under this effect inflicts Tune Strain - Shifting, they gain 40% DMG Amplification instead.

This effect ends early when this Resonator is switched out or when Denia switches modes.

skills.name: Shattered Hours
skills.description:
When the target's Off-Tune Level is full, Denia can cast Tune Break on the target.

When in Resonance Mode - Tune Strain, Denia gains the following effects:

  • Denia can inflict Tune Strain - Shifting on the target.

  • Denia can respond to Tune Strain - Interfered.

When responding to Tune Strain - Interfered: For each stack of Tune Strain - Interfered on the target, each point of Denia's Tune Break Boost increases her total DMG against the target by 0.12%.

While Denia is in the team, the max stack limit of Tune Strain - Interfered on a target is increased by 1.

Yinlin's Signature is the usual generalist weapon of choice for any Rectifier damage dealer, and Denia can definitely rely on it for great results as well even if this weapon lacks team buffing capabilities like her Signature.

Another very strong generalist Rectifier option with a particularly high Base ATK and reduced potential in Tune Strain teams due to not activating the DEF Ignore part of the passive until the very end of the rotation.
Simple ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for Denia, who does not benefit from this weapon's Spectro Frazzle-related effects.
Simple ATK and CRIT DMG stat-stick for Denia, who barely benefits from this weapon's Basic and Havoc DMG-related effects.
Simple ATK and CRIT DMG stat-stick for Denia, who doesn't benefit from this weapon's Basic DMG-related effects.

Best permanently available option for Denia. Grants some Energy Regen and massive ATK boosts, but the lack of a CRIT stat definitely makes for a big gap between this weapon and her Signature. Still better than any 4-star by virtue of a much higher Base ATK.

This Battle Pass exclusive grants Denia a solid ATK buff upon casting Ultimate, alongside a CRIT secondary stat albeit with very low Base ATK which makes it pale in comparison to the likes of her Signature (or any 5-star for that matter), but still a viable weapon overall.
This Battle Pass exclusive grants Denia a small ATK% boost upon casting her Skill and some Basic DMG that she doesn't care for. Lower than most weapons due to low Base ATK, much like any 4-star.

Best no-gacha option for Denia in Fusion Burst mode, granting her a huge ATK boost but no other stats, making it a weaker version of Cosmic Ripples. Practically useless in Tune Strain mode because Denia won't activate the passive then.
Grants some extra flat Energy upon casting Skill, but has no noteworthy stats beyond that. Weak 4-star that only grants lower quantities of ATK overall, not recommended.
Best no-gacha option for Denia in Tune Strain mode, accessible from the start, grants a decent amount of ATK to get started on the game but should be replaced ASAP.

echoes.Comment: Best generalist option in Fusion Burst mode, grants Denia with 20% total Fusion Burst DMG increase for a small personal damage gain and most importantly a total of 37% Fusion DMG Bonus (including Main Echo) to the incoming character via Outro. Best mix of personal damage and buffing generally.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Summon Echo that gives 12% Fusion DMG Bonus to the incoming character via Outro, adding to the 25% from the base set for a total of 37% Fusion DMG buff on Outro.

echoes.Comment: Best option in Tune Strain mode, gives a 10% self-ATK buff on the 2-piece and also a 20 Tune Break Boost buff team-wide which comes in handy to maximize on DMG Taken effects from Tune Strain.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Transform Echo that can safely be cast at the very end of Denia's rotation before Outro, giving an extra 12% ATK buff to the incoming character.

echoes.Comment: Best choice for Denia in the Aemeath + Lupa team, with Lupa on Moonlit Clouds, in order to give the highest possible buffs to Aemeath via Lupa's Outro while maximizing on party-wide buffing and Denia's personal DMG.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Summon Echo that gives 12% Fusion and 12% Liberation DMG Bonus when equipped in the main slot, useful for maximizing further on Denia's personal damage.

teams.Comments: Teammate alternatives to Mornye are not listed as you will experience very significant team DPS drop-offs when trying to replace her, making it not recommended to use Denia in Tune Strain mode without Mornye.

synergies.Comment: Best and only DPS choice for Fusion Burst Denia, together with Aemeath they form one of the strongest teams in the entire game, excelling in both AoE and singletarget damage with a fast and easy rotation and a low reliance on Signature weapons to perform, with the only caveat being they're somewhat stranded for Supports with only Chisa and Lupa being able to draw out the team's full potential. Still, Aemeath is the main reason to be getting and using Denia and makes for a ridiculously strong team.

Denia in Tune Strain mode is the best in slot partner for both Qingxiao and Luuk if Mornye is available to use alongside the 2 of them, making their mid-air single-target oriented combat less clunky in Whimpering Wastes thanks to Denia's constant off-field grouping, as well as overall just being their highest-damaging team composition for all situations. Note however that Denia experiences significant team DPS drop-offs without Mornye available as a Support and is overall not recommended for Tune Strain without Mornye involved.

3rd slot options for Denia teams depending on what team she's ran in. Chisa is ideal with Aemeath but Lupa is an excellent fallback with alternative Echo set choices which will draw just about the same performance as Chisa. Mornye on the other hand is best for Tune Strain Denia teams while providing nothing of value to Aemeath.
